Container.Name: isputnik-video
Container.Overview:
The video engine for isputnik.home, in a container of its own: TV shows and movies scanned from your video folders, laid out the way Jellyfin and Kodi read them, described from .nfo files and TMDB (posters, backdrops, cast, sets of films, genres), and played in the browser and in the iSputnik TV app. A file a browser plays as it is goes as it is; the rest is converted while it plays, on the CPU or on an Intel CPU's graphics, with HDR tone-mapped and Blu-ray subtitles drawn in. Each person resumes where they stopped, intros and credits are skipped, viewers away from home are held under a quality cap. Everything runs on your server; nothing is sent anywhere.
This is an add-on for isputnik.home and does nothing on its own: it has no sign-in and no pages. Install it beside the isputnik container; video libraries are added, shared and watched in isputnik.home. Set it up from isputnik.home, on Control panel, Settings, Apps, Video. Before installing, press Generate secret there and copy it (it is shown once); paste it into the Gateway Secret field below, which is required. Give the container your video share as Video Folders (read-only: the engine never writes to it). Once it runs, enter its address on the same page (http://[your Unraid IP]:4300 as installed here) and press Test connection, which then says Paired. Then add a library under Control panel, Library, Libraries, Add library, Video. Needs isputnik.home 4.38 or newer.
Container.Changes:
### 2026.11.13 — 0.38.1 Diagnostics, released - **0.38.0 reaches the image.** It was never published: a test that runs before the image is built looked at the conversion's memory and disk once, right as a new segment sat on the disk on its way into memory, and failed. It now waits for that moment to pass. This release carries everything in 0.38.0: the engine's part of home's diagnostics report (home 4.89.0), and the GPU's recent failures kept with ffmpeg's own words.
### 2026.11.12 — 0.38.0 Diagnostics for bug reports - **The engine reports on itself for a bug report.** Home's new Control panel › Infrastructure › Diagnostics page asks it for its version and machine, the ffmpeg it runs, what the GPU check found, its conversion settings, its libraries' counts and states, and the warnings and errors in its log. Home hides names, folders and addresses unless the admin asks to include them, and nothing leaves home unless the admin copies the report out. Needs isputnik.home 4.89.0 to be seen. - **The GPU's recent failures are kept with ffmpeg's own words.** The last ten, each with when it happened and whether it counted towards setting the GPU aside (a film without HDR mastering data doesn't). Before, only the count was kept, so a report of "the GPU isn't used" came with nothing to go on.
### 2026.11.12 — 0.37.1 Posters past a sleeping disk - **Scrolling past posters no longer waits on a sleeping disk.** A poster or backdrop kept beside a film was looked up in a way that held the whole engine, so a page of posters from a disk that had spun down stopped everyone, people watching something else included, until it was up again. It is now looked up without holding anything, as the films themselves have been since 0.37.0. - **A poster taken away from beside its film is simply not there.** One removed after the engine had found it answered with an error; it now answers that there is no such picture.
### 2026.11.12 — 0.37.0 Answers through every scan - **The engine keeps answering while it scans.** A scan read the whole library in one go and nothing else got a turn until it finished: on a big library on a NAS share that was minutes with no health check, no page and no video, and the container showed as unhealthy. The disk is now read a little at a time between other work, and the catalog written from it in one short step. A library a stop left marked as queued or scanning is set back on start. - **No more minutes of silence after a scan.** The pass that looks for posters and TMDB details went over every title after every scan, rewrote each one even when nothing had changed, and worked its cast and crew out again from scratch. It now writes only what changed, works out the cast only of titles that got new people, lists each folder once, and lets other work in between titles. Scanning the cast of the whole catalog, which the scan did too, is now done only for titles added, removed or with another cast in their .nfo. On a test library of 2000 films the engine stopped answering for about 10 seconds per scan; now for well under one. - **A sleeping disk no longer stops everyone.** Finding a film's file, the subtitles beside it and its .edl waited on the disk in a way that held the whole engine: when the disk holding one film had spun down, people watching something else waited for it too. Those lookups now wait on their own. The folder picker in Add library, and finding intros and credits after a scan, do the same. - **Intros and credits are looked for when nobody is watching.** That work went on while someone watched a converted film, taking cores and disk from them. It now waits between seasons and films while someone is watching, as copies for download already did. Find again from home still runs at once. - **Switching quality mid-film no longer restarts the conversion over and over.** A segment of the old quality still on its way stopped the new one's conversion to start its own, and the two took turns, about 20 times in two seconds. The quality whose playlist the player asked for last is now the one being played, and a late request for another is turned away without being asked again. - **Films played before 0.31.0 no longer read the whole file again.** Probing a film again for what 0.31.0 added threw away where its keyframes are, though the file had not changed, so each such film's next play had to read it all through. They are now kept while the file stays the same. - **HDR films can be tone-mapped on an Intel GPU.** The start-up check always said the GPU could not tone-map, because its test picture carried none of the mastering details an HDR10 film has and the GPU refuses a picture without them. The test picture has them now. HLG films, which usually carry none, are tone-mapped on the CPU, and a film the GPU refuses for want of them goes to the CPU without counting against the GPU. - **Backups are taken a little at a time.** The catalog was copied for a backup in one piece in memory; it is now copied with SQLite's own backup between other work and streamed to home, and the copy a restore keeps for undoing it is made the same way.
### 2026.11.12 — 0.36.1 Released for real - **0.35.0 and 0.36.0 reach the image at last.** Neither was published: the tests that run before the image is built failed, because the ffmpeg they used (a separate build, not the one the image ships) crashed whenever it put an MPEG-TS video into an MP4, which is how a copy for download is finished. The tests now use the same kind of ffmpeg as the image. This release carries everything in 0.35.0 (converting in memory unless /transcode is a disk, one shared conversion, films kept once converted, Keep ready) and 0.36.0 (big films start sooner). - **A copy for download is put together from one stream.** Its kept pieces are now handed to ffmpeg one after another rather than through a list file: simpler, and nothing left behind if it stops.
Container.Requires: Needs the isputnik (isputnik.home) container, version 4.38 or newer, installed on the same server. The engine is reached only through it.

Config.Name: Engine Port
Config.Description: The port the isputnik container reaches the engine on: enter http://[your Unraid IP]:[this port] as the Video address in isputnik.home (Control panel, Settings, Apps). Not for browsers: video is watched inside isputnik.home. On br0 with a fixed IP, or on a user-defined network shared with the isputnik container, this mapping is not used and the address is the container's own IP or name with port 4300.

Config.Name: Config & Data
Config.Description: Stores the catalog: shows, seasons, episodes and movies found in the video folders, posters and each person's progress (a SQLite database and a picture cache). Keep it apart from the isputnik container's appdata. isputnik.home's backups include a copy of the database.

Config.Name: Video Folders
Config.Description: The share that holds your shows and movies, mounted read-only: the engine never writes to it. Each video library is a folder under it, for example Shows or Movies, chosen in isputnik.home when the library is added.

Config.Name: Transcode
Config.Description: Optional fast disk for video: conversion that overflows memory, and copies prepared for download. Point it at a cache-pool or SSD folder. Left empty, video is converted in memory only and no copies are prepared; how much memory is set in the app (Videos › Settings).

Config.Name: Intel GPU
Config.Description: Optional. /dev/dri to convert video on an Intel CPU's graphics (Quick Sync) instead of the CPU: several viewers at once for little CPU. Leave empty to convert on the CPU. Settings, Video in isputnik.home shows what was found.

Config.Name: Gateway Secret
Config.Description: The secret isputnik.home signs its requests with, so this engine knows who is signed in. Make it first, in isputnik.home on Control panel, Settings, Apps, Video (Generate secret; it is shown once), and paste it here. Required: the engine refuses to start without one, or with one shorter than 32 characters. Everything else about video is managed inside isputnik.home.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the engine runs as. It runs unprivileged (not root); on first start it takes ownership of the Config & Data path as this user. This user must be able to read the Video Folders. 99 (nobody) matches the default owner of an Unraid share.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the engine runs as. 100 (users) matches the default group of an Unraid share.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal or silent. isputnik.home shows this log and the engine's own event record under Control panel, Overview, Logs.
